MAJOR: in_scope declares "EAP manifest asset bundle integration" and config_contract names config/eap-registry.json, but neither affected_files nor affected_components includes it (CL-016); the approved in-scope change is outside the declared file set.

SPA fallback precedence vs API routing unspecified: without an explicit mount/prefix contract excluding API paths, unknown /api/* requests can return index.html 200 instead of JSON 404, silently breaking downstream API error contracts.
[OUT_OF_SCOPE] Prior MAJOR/BLOCKER items remain disposition=PENDING; per CL-006, Gate 1 approval is invalid until they are addressed — noted here only as a gate status, not re-reported.
MINOR: Rollback path PF_CONSOLE_STATIC_DIR serves from disk; parity of traversal protection, cache/gzip headers, and integrity verification with the embedded path is unspecified, so the rollback can weaken AC-2 guarantees.
Packaging validator exposes only fail-closed exit-1 behavior; no report-only/dry-run mode for local developers (guardrail 4: blast radius/dry-run for build-time gates).
No stated binary-size budget or CI size check despite the declared size-increase risk; embed growth is unbounded without a threshold.
No surfaced console bundle build metadata (version/SHA in EAP manifest or a health/readiness field) to correlate a running binary with a specific asset bundle during support and incident triage.
NIT: SPA_FALLBACK_OK logged per request can be high-volume; prefer debug-level or sampled logging for fallback successes.
"500 for internal read error" is effectively unreachable with embed.FS (reads fail only as not-found); clarify the 404-vs-500 mapping to avoid a dead/untestable branch.
SUMMARY: Design is directionally sound (Go embed, fail-closed IP guard, deterministic hashed assets) and AC traceability is largely complete, but Gate 1 cannot proceed: the EAP-manifest in-scope change is missing from declared files, SPA-fallback route precedence against the API mux is unspecified (API error-contract risk), and all prior PENDING findings still block approval under CL-006.
Top risks to close: scope declaration for config/eap-registry.json, fallback/API route ordering, and behavioral parity of the rollback external-directory path.
